questions.q: In Oracle Fusion, how is access actually granted to a person?
options: Directly to their user account by an administrator
By provisioning a role to their user account
By adding them to a database table of approved users
Automatically, based on their email domain
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion never grants access directly to a user. Access is granted to a role, and a person receives it only when that role is provisioned to their account.

questions.q: What is a privilege in the Oracle Fusion security model?
options: A named user account with elevated rights
A report that lists every role in the system
The smallest grantable unit of permission to perform one specific action
A synonym for a job role
questions.explain: A privilege is the smallest unit of 'permission to do one thing,' such as voiding a payment. Privileges are granted to roles, not directly to users.

questions.q: A user can open the Create Invoice page but sees zero invoices when the page loads. Which security layer most likely explains this?
options: Function security, because they can't open the page
Data security, because function security passed but no data security policy matches their rows
The user account itself is disabled
The invoice module is not installed
questions.explain: Passing function security (being able to open a page) and passing data security (seeing rows) are separate checks. Opening the page but seeing nothing points to data security.

questions.q: Which tool is used to view, build, and provision roles in Oracle Fusion?
options: Functional Setup Manager
Business Intelligence Publisher
The Chart of Accounts workbook
The Security Console
questions.explain: The Security Console is the central tool for viewing and comparing roles, building custom roles, and provisioning roles to users.

questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion grant access to roles instead of directly to individual users?
options: So that when a person changes jobs or leaves, access can be managed by changing role provisioning rather than rebuilding permissions from scratch
Because roles are faster to type than usernames
Because direct user grants are technically impossible in any software
Because only roles can be assigned a password
questions.explain: Granting access to roles rather than users means a replacement hire simply gets provisioned the same role, inheriting consistent access without rebuilding permissions by hand.
